matchstick.title: Compute numeric discrepancy
matchstick.principle: Convert each Roman numeral in the equation to its integer value, then evaluate the left‑hand side and the right‑hand side (including the operator) to see how far they differ. The size and sign of the discrepancy tell you which side must be increased or decreased.
matchstick.when_to_apply: At the start of solving any matchstick equation, before trying any moves.

matchstick.title: Enumerate single‑stick numeral transformations
matchstick.principle: List all Roman‑numeral characters that can be obtained by moving a single stick from or to a given character while preserving its orientation (e.g., I↔II, V↔X). This yields the pool of candidate one‑stick changes.
matchstick.when_to_apply: After computing the discrepancy, generate possible transformations for each character.
matchstick.example: From I you can add a vertical stick to make II; from V you can reposition a diagonal to make X.

matchstick.title: Validate source and destination characters
matchstick.principle: When a stick is removed from a source character, the remaining sticks must still form a valid Roman numeral or operator; after adding the stick to the destination, that character must also be valid. Invalid intermediate symbols are not allowed.
matchstick.when_to_apply: For each candidate move generated in enumeration, check both the source and destination for validity before accepting the move.
matchstick.example: Removing a vertical from II yields I (valid); adding that vertical to a plus sign turns it into a minus sign (valid).

matchstick.title: V↔X transformation (reposition diagonal)
matchstick.principle: By moving one diagonal stick of a V so that it crosses the other diagonal, you turn V (5) into X (10); moving a diagonal away from an X can create a V, changing the value by ±5.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the equation contains a V or X and the numeric discrepancy suggests a change of five.
matchstick.example: Changing V in IV to X yields IX, increasing the value from 4 to 9 (+5).

matchstick.title: I↔II vertical addition/removal
matchstick.principle: Adding a vertical stick to an I creates II (value +1); removing a vertical stick from II yields I (value –1). This is the only way to change a numeral by one using a vertical stick.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the discrepancy is ±1 or when a vertical stick can be transferred to or from an I/II.
matchstick.example: Turning II into III by moving a vertical stick from a plus sign to the numeral.

matchstick.title: Operator change: – to + (or + to –)
matchstick.principle: Adding a vertical stick to a minus sign creates a plus sign, turning subtraction into addition (RHS changes by +2 × right operand). Removing the vertical stick from a plus sign makes a minus sign, turning addition into subtraction (RHS changes by –2 × right operand).
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the equation contains a plus or minus and the numeric discrepancy matches the effect of flipping the operator.
matchstick.example: Removing the vertical from '+' in XIV + XI turns it into '–', reducing RHS by 2 × 11 = 22.

matchstick.title: Never alter the equality sign
matchstick.principle: The '=' sign must remain exactly two horizontal sticks; moving any stick away destroys the equality operator and is prohibited.
matchstick.when_to_apply: For every candidate move, ensure the equality sign is untouched.
matchstick.example: Do not take a horizontal stick from '=' to change a numeral.

matchstick.title: Respect stick orientation
matchstick.principle: Sticks retain their orientation; a diagonal stick cannot be used as a vertical stick and vice versa. Transformations must keep each stick’s angle unchanged.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When considering a move, verify that the stick’s orientation matches the target character’s required orientation.
matchstick.example: A diagonal stick from X cannot be placed to form an I.

matchstick.title: Re‑evaluate arithmetic after each move
matchstick.principle: After applying a candidate stick relocation, recompute the integer values of the whole equation to verify that it now holds; discard moves that do not produce a valid equality.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Immediately after any proposed transformation, before finalizing the answer.
matchstick.example: After moving the vertical from '+' to II, recompute LHS = 3, RHS = 14 – 11 = 3, confirming correctness.

matchstick.title: Operator‑numeral combined move
matchstick.principle: When a plus sign contains a vertical stick, moving that stick to an I (or II) simultaneously turns the plus into a minus and changes the numeral’s value by ±1. This yields a net arithmetic adjustment of +1 on the side containing the numeral and –2 × right‑operand on the side of the operator, often resolving small discrepancies.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the discrepancy can be expressed as the sum of a ±1 numeral change and the effect of flipping the operator (±2 × right operand), consider transferring the vertical stick from the operator to the numeral.
matchstick.example: II = XIV + XI → move the vertical from '+' to the left‑hand II, giving III = XIV – XI, which balances (3 = 3).

matchstick.description: Treating a diagonal stick as a vertical I
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model forgets that stick orientation is fixed and tries to use a diagonal to form a vertical line.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Always check the orientation of the stick before assigning it to a character; diagonals can only form V, X, etc., never I.

matchstick.why_it_happens: The model assumes any stick can be moved, overlooking the rule that '=' must stay as two horizontal sticks.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Explicitly exclude the equality sign from source or destination candidates in every move.

matchstick.description: Leaving an invalid source character after removal
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model removes a stick without verifying that the remaining strokes still form a valid Roman numeral or operator.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: After removing a stick, immediately validate that the leftover shape corresponds to a legal character.

matchstick.why_it_happens: The model overlooks that moving a vertical stick can change a plus to a minus (or vice versa), missing a powerful way to adjust the arithmetic.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: When a plus or minus is present, always consider the effect of adding or removing its vertical stick as a possible move.

matchstick.description: Skipping arithmetic verification after a visual change
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model focuses on the visual correctness of characters but forgets to recompute the equation’s numeric value.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Re‑evaluate the whole equation’s integer values after each candidate move before accepting it.
